title: HAL_FLASHEx_OBProgram erases write protection if read protection is also selected
body:
This is more of a code-review style bug report, so I skip the unnecessary administration.

`HAL_FLASHEx_OBProgram` calls `FLASH_OB_EnableWRP` or `FLASH_OB_DisableWRP` when write protection options are passed into it. Afterwards it calls `FLASH_OB_RDP_LevelConfig` if read protection options are passed into it. All 3 of these internal methods perform an OB erase, so when write and read protection are both selected, then

1. OB is erased
2. write protection bits are written into OB
3. OB is erased
4. read protection byte is written into OB

So the write protection bits aren't applied as intended.

comments.author: MKISTM
comments.body:
Hello @benedekkupper,

Thank you for your report, i believe this behavior is correct.

According to the [STM32F10xxx XL-density Flash programming](https://www.st.com/resource/en/programming_manual/pm0068-stm32f10xxx-xldensity-flash-programming-stmicroelectronics.pdf) manuel **page 19**

> On every system reset, the option byte loader (OBL) reads the information block and stores 
> the data into the Option byte register (FLASH_OBR) and the Write protection register 
> (FLASH_WRPR). Each option byte also has its complement in the information block. 
> During option loading, by verifying the option bit and its complement, it is possible to check that the 
> loading has correctly taken place. If this is not the case, an option byte error (OPTERR) is 
> generated. When a comparison error occurs the corresponding option byte is forced to 
> 0xFF. The comparator is disabled when the option byte and its complement are both equal 
> to 0xFF (Electrical Erase state).

Please do not hesitate to ask if anything is unclear, and keep me informed

BR,
Mohamed Chaker.

title: STM32F1xx RTC BKP Registers 16bit, but HAL requests 32bits
body:
I'm fairly new to MCU development and working with the STM32F1xx series, but I've been pointed over to here from the STM32duino project as they pull the HAL from here.

The RTC BKP registers on the STM32F103 (and I believe all of the STM32F1xx series) are 16bit, but the HAL driver (Inc/stm32f1xx_ll_rtc.h) requests and accepts an unsigned 32bit value. Of course it can't actually save 32bits only 16bits, so you lose the top 16bits of the data you sent. 

Obviously it is possible to work around this by splitting the data over 2 registers, but is this by design? Perhaps there is an MCU in the series that has a 32bit backup register and I've missed it? In my opinion, if all MCUs in the series have 16bit RTC BKP registers, the HAL should request and accept just 16bits to avoid confusion and accidental data loss.

comments.author: ALABSTM
comments.body:
Hi @RedEchidnaUK,

Thank you for this proposal. However, looking at page **86** of [RM0008](https://www.st.com/content/ccc/resource/technical/document/reference_manual/59/b9/ba/7f/11/af/43/d5/CD00171190.pdf/files/CD00171190.pdf/jcr:content/translations/en.CD00171190.pdf), revision 21, you would notice that the backup registers are actually **32-bit wide**, with the 16 MSB being **reserved** (screenshot below).

![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f1xx_hal_driver/assets/46019491/5a4f3927-bc00-4704-99ea-4b9439a62531)

These 16 reserved bits are simply **not** represented on page **83** (screenshot below).

![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f1xx_hal_driver/assets/46019491/b4587f8d-8bec-49c5-addb-3eb2ac792af5)

Now, regarding the accidental data loss, I guess you mean storing a 32-bit wide data in one of the backup registers and, thus, having the 16 MSB lost as coinciding with the reserved part of the register. In this case, it is up to the user to pay attention.

One last comment, if I may.
* As the STM32F1xx microcontrollers are 32-bit microcontrollers, data is "manipulated" in "chunks" of 32 bits.
  * This data should hence be stored in memory (particularly RAM), at addresses **multiple of** 32 bits or 4 bytes (**e.g.**, 0x2000'0000, 0x2000'0004).
  * This is what we call data **alignment** in memory.
* In case of 16-bit wide data, it would be stored at addresses 0x2000'0000 and 0x2000'0002.
  * Supposing the CPU of a 32-bit microcontroller would fetch the data at address 0x2000'0000, the data at address 0x2000'0002 would be fetched along with it and **extra operations** would be needed to separate both. This would result in a **loss of performance**.
  * Moreover, if the CPU would fetch the data at address 0x2000'0002, it would be unable to do it as this would yield a **fault** due to an **unaligned** memory access.
  * To close this comment, there is this interesting note at page **49**.

![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f1xx_hal_driver/assets/46019491/d168873b-d183-4c56-b896-85232350b885)

I hope this helps. I let you dig deeper into this topic. Thank you again for your proposal. Please allow me to close this issue.

With regards,

comments.author: RedEchidnaUK
comments.body: Thank you for the detailed explanation.

title: Interrupting USB Transfer
body:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f1xx_hal_driver/blob/ddf259a6eb9dc4ba421f5e2b1ae619bd77468214/Inc/stm32f1xx_hal_pcd.h#L868

This line of code is interrupting my USB Transfer in random time on STM32F103.
In Wireshark i see the OUT Endpoint answered with USBD_STATUS_STALL_PID

The host is continously sending Data to the OUT Pipe.
While debugging the **HAL_PCD_EP_Receive** , until this line of code, the connection is stable.
Stepping over it will interrupt the Transaction and on Host the Pipe is broken.

In normal running, the next line in Debug, will reactivate the Pipe to valid state, so the host is not recognizing it.
But some interrupts occour within this two lines and the transfer is broken.
The two lines are part of **USB_EPStartXfer**:
 - 2441: PCD_SET_EP_RX_CNT(USBx, ep->num, len);
 - 2467: PCD_SET_EP_RX_STATUS(USBx, ep->num, USB_EP_RX_VALID);

After deleting this line, i had no transfer interruptions any more.

comments.author: AndyD87
comments.body:
The 0x3FFU is generating an PMA Overrun wich is resulting in an stalled OUT Endpoint.

The Host is running a WinUSB Driver wich could not handle this Error State.
A pipe reset was required to continue the transfer.

The STM32F1 is running wihtout any peripherals, just USB and the HSE Oscilator was activated with CubeMX.
The USB Part was configured with 1 OUT and 1 IN EP with 64 Byte of maximum packet size for Bulktransfer.
The STM32F1 Application was reduced to a while(1) which is coninously calling HAL_PCD_EP_Receive and a short timeout of 1ms to simulate the data handling.
The Error happend on different devices.

Hi @AndyD87,

Replying to what you posted
>> The STM32F1 Application was reduced to a while(1) which is coninously calling HAL_PCD_EP_Receive and a short timeout of 1ms to simulate the data handling. 

Our development teams said this is not the way to program a USB transfer as this will necessarily break the ongoing transfer. Instead you should check that the current transfer has been completed (using the one the below callback , for instance) before submitting any new Rx transfer. A simple `while(1)` loop cannot allow that.

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f1xx_hal_driver/blob/e0654977ea5d79a4bee5f153f62d53bf2e376602/Src/stm32f1xx_hal_pcd.c#L2372-L2377

With regards,

title: Changing the write-only AFIO_MAPR.SWJ_CFG field in LL
body:
In stm32f1xx_ll_gpio.h, LL_GPIO_AF_EnableRemap_SWJ(), LL_GPIO_AF_Remap_SWJ_NONJTRST, LL_GPIO_AF_Remap_SWJ_NOJTAG(), LL_GPIO_AF_DisableRemap_SWJ() all use

`SET_BIT(AFIO->MAPR, AFIO_MAPR_SWJ_CFG_xxxxx);`

which is incorrect, as SET_BIT is

`#define SET_BIT(REG, BIT) ((REG) |= (BIT))`

and the read value of AFIO_MAPR.SWJ_CFG field according to RM0008 is unpredictable.

This has been reported in https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus-embedded-software/incorrectly-written-afio-mapr-swj-cfg-bits-in-cubef1-ll/m-p/90756 , can you please drop a comment there, too.

Thanks,

Jan Waclawek

HAL_StatusTypeDef HAL_FLASHEx_Erase_IT(FLASH_EraseInitTypeDef *pEraseInit)
{
  HAL_StatusTypeDef status = HAL_OK;

  /* Process Locked */
  __HAL_LOCK(&pFlash);

  /* If procedure already ongoing, reject the next one */

title: A bug when use HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA
body:
**Describe the bug**
Cannot distinguish between half complete in DMA and idle interrupts

**How To Reproduce**
1. set a rxSize

2. use HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA

3. send half the data （rxSize/2）

4. HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback will be called 2 times with the same input parameter(size)

comments.author: KORKAD
comments.body:
Hello @rzzuozuo

This is the normal behavior for this UART service:

     Use of HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA service, will generate calls to
     user defined HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback callback for each occurrence of
     following events :
     - DMA RX Half Transfer event (HT)
     - DMA RX Transfer Complete event (TC)
     - IDLE event on UART Rx line (indicating a pause is UART reception flow)

for more details please refer to the [UART_ReceptionToIdle_CircularDMA](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/tree/master/Projects/STM32446E-Nucleo/Examples/UART/UART_ReceptionToIdle_CircularDMA) example available on STM32CubeF4 package.

title: SetPinMode and SetPinPull sequence

comments.author: ASELSTM
comments.body:
Hi @mgiaco,

First, we would like to thank you for your contribution.

Actually, this change aims to correct the GPIO initialization sequence to avoid unwanted pulse on GPIO Pin’s. Indeed, old configuration sequence

```

1. Pin Mode configuration
2. Pull-up Pull-down resistor configuration
3. Speed mode configuration
4. Output mode configuration

```
causes unwanted pulse generation when initializing of the GPIO registers leading to an incorrect behavior. This sequence has therefore been corrected to avoid this case. The new sequence is then such as updated in the latest release.

```

1. Speed mode configuration
2. Output mode configuration
3. Pull-up Pull-down resistor configuration
4. Pin Mode configuration

```
 
The fix was also mentioned in the [Release Note](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f1xx_hal_driver/blob/master/Release_Notes.html) under **"HAL/LL GPIO driver"** section as following : 

> Update LL GPIO initialization sequence to avoid unwanted pulse on GPIO Pin’s

Hope this has given you a better understanding of the fix.

With regards,
